This subject equips students with a rigorous understanding of portfolio analysis through quantitative tools.

It covers a comprehensive mathematical treatment of the Markowitz framework for portfolio optimization, the index-tracking problem, Arbitrage Pricing Theory (APT) and factor models for asset pricing, portfolio performance measurement, portfolio risk measures, and capital allocation.
The subject also tackles a continuous-time portfolio optimization problem (the Merton problem) via a stochastic optimal control approach.
The theoretical discussion of concepts is complemented by practical problems involving statistical estimation and computational implementation.

The first module will discuss the fundamental concepts of artificial neural systems and fuzzy logic theory.
It introduces the foundations of neural network learning principles including the Hebbian, Perceptron, Delta, and Widrow-Hoff learning rules.
It includes fuzzy sets, linguistic variables and approximate reasoning.
The second module covers the concept of error function 3eneralized3 using the steepest descent 3eneralized3 technique.
This will then be extended to multilayer feedforward neural networks.
Other concepts such as 3eneralized delta learning rule, feedforward recall and error back-propagation training, associative memories, matching and self-organising networks will be discussed.
Further topics will include the preliminaries and basic construction of a fuzzy controller, adaptive fuzzy logic controller, and the self-organising fuzzy logic controller.
Lastly, a basic concept of convolutional neural network and genetic algorithm are introduced.
The third module relates to advanced applications of intelligent systems.
The design and development of a semi-autonomous wheelchair using neural network classifications will be discussed.
Other advanced applications relate to the control of blood glucose in patients with diabetes using a fuzzy system.
This subject introduces you to neural networks and fuzzy theory with an engineering focus, offering hands-on experience and professional practice integration.
You'll learn how these intelligent systems can identify and control dynamic systems without pre-existing models, using numerical and linguistic data to learn and adapt.
Through practical examples, you'll develop expertise in applying neural networks and fuzzy logic to real-world engineering applications.

This subject is intended for students in the Master of Data Science and Innovation ( C04372 ) who are in their final stage of the course and have 2 credit points remaining to complete the course with 96 credit points.
The study load of this subject is about 3-4 hours per week, or about 35 hours in total, for one assignment.
It can be taken as an online self-study course or as a small project.
In either case, the topic should be related to data science.
Example of project: sentiment analysis of political autobiographies.
Example of online self-study: data wrangling with pandas.
For the small project, an academic advisor needs to be organised by the student.
Any UTS faculty, or a suitably qualified external professional can be the advisor.
At the beginning of the semester, students write a one-page proposal including the assessment task, for which the academic advisor has agreed to supervise and assess the work.
For the online self-study course, it should include assessment tasks with a certificate of completion.

This subject provides a 140 to 160-hour Data Science internship, allowing you to apply your data science knowledge within a real-world business project.
You'll work within a professional team, under a host organisation's supervision, on projects ranging from research to data analysis or consultancy, either solo or collaboratively.
A learning contract detailing tasks, goals, and timelines will be crafted between you and your host supervisor and approved by the subject coordinator.
Your assessment includes reporting on the internship's outcomes and reflecting on your internship's experience, enhancing your understanding of Data Science in practice.
Enrolment is contingent on securing an internship and obtaining approval via e-request on CareerHub.
